question.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $4x-5>9$ or $3<10x+8<16.$
question.worked_solution:
We start by solving $4x-5>9:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-5 & >9 \\ 4x & >14 \\ x & >\frac{14}{4} \\ x & >\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/e39459442837c3de83da860526c5f39b048d02b33b6ea0a3340efd599bb880d3.png)

Then, we solve $3<10x+8<16:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & <10x+8<16 \\ 3-8 & <10x<16-8 \\ -5 & <10x<8 \\ -\frac{5}{10} & <x<\frac{8}{10} \\ -\frac{1}{2} & <x<\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/611944fd64cf3638f0cfd4ae8f8a658496af927adc7b91f68e7aafdd36817272.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/112f50397f85c79e51650d88d2d4125cdb5479e60af579836bc3c8cd4eb22276.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x>\frac{7}{2}$ or $-\frac{1}{2}<x<\frac{4}{5}.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{4}{5})\cup (\frac{7}{2},\infty ).
$$
